title: Split Array with Equal Sum
summary: Given an integer array nums of length n, determine if there exists a triplet (i, j, k) such that 0 < i < i + 1 < j < j + 1 < k < n - 1 and the sum of the subarrays (0, i - 1), (i + 1, j - 1), (j + 1, k - 1), and (k + 1, n - 1) are equal.
statement: Given an integer array nums of length n, determine if there exists a triplet (i, j, k) such that 0 < i < i + 1 < j < j + 1 < k < n - 1 and the sum of the subarrays (0, i - 1), (i + 1, j - 1), (j + 1, k - 1), and (k + 1, n - 1) are equal.
constraints: Remove indices i,j,k with at least one element in each of the four remaining sections.
hints: Fix the middle removed index j and match feasible sums from its left and right sides.
For each j, collect sums where the first two sections match.
Search k on the right; accept when its two sections match and their sum occurs in the left set.
Every valid triple has one middle j and is tested, while prefix sums make each section comparison constant time.
editorial: Every valid triple has one middle j and is tested, while prefix sums make each section comparison constant time.

tests.explanation: Removing indices 1,3,5 leaves four sections each summing to one.
No three separators produce four equal section sums.
